title: Weighted influence lower bound
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one vector and is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $T$ be a decision tree whose queries are restricted to coordinates in $A$. If $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ takes only the values $-1$ and $1$, then half the sum, over all coordinates, of the product of the probability that $T$ queries that coordinate and the product influence of $f$ at that coordinate is at least the smaller of the probabilities that $f$ equals $1$ and $-1$, minus the error probability of $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
$B$ is a real basis of functions on $\Omega$
$B$ is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
$A$ is a set of coordinates in $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
$T$ is a decision tree on the coordinates in $A$
